items.title: The Blue Wave Has Tech Bros Scrambling for Data Centers in Space
items.summary: After Democrats won big in Texas and other AI infrastructure hot spots on Tuesday, data center enthusiasts looked for comfort in low Earth orbit.
items.content:
A wave of Democratic candidates across the country —and notably in Texas, a national data center hotspot and home to Elon Musk’s SpaceX—won their state and congressional races on Tuesday, including many candidates who voiced opposition to the data center industry . The results have sent some corners of the tech industry looking to the heavens for answers.

In recent hours, data center enthusiasts have proclaimed on social media that they’re still “ bullish ” on building data centers—just not necessarily in Texas, or even on Earth at all. Instead, they say, it’s time to focus on data centers in space.

Elon Musk—who sank more than $400 million of his fortune supporting Republican candidates who all went on to lose their midterms races—has been among those leading the charge. “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Musk posted on X in the early hours of Wednesday, after it was clear that Democrats had taken the House and Senate.

Jordan Lasker— the man behind the X account "Crémieux,” which is a popular follow in the tech world, and known for posting race-based pseudoscience—also weighed in, saying , “Data centers in space are an incredible idea and anyone who doubted them didn't think enough about tonight's election results.”

Throughout the day, Musk employees , tech investors , AI researchers , venture capitalists , and industry fans joined the chorus of support for space-based data centers. Soham Mehta, a research fellow at the techno-optimist think tank Foundation for American Innovation, argued that underwater data centers should also be considered. (In June, China began operating what it claims is the world’s first underwater data center.)

Some companies are already trying to put compute in orbit. Among them are Google, which launched a satellite that it says contains "data center class TPU,” and SpaceX, which says it aims to deploy “thousands of AI satellites starting as soon as late 2027.” Blue Origin is also in the mix, having filed for a Federal Communications Commission permit to launch 50,000 satellites that will constitute an “orbital data center system.”

There are also a few startups aiming to build data centers in space, including Starcloud, which claims to have carried "the first NVIDIA H100 GPU into orbit" in November 2025.

Despite being technically possible, the realities of in-orbit data centers are difficult . Among other things, space-based data centers are much more expensive than land-based ones, can’t grow to hyperscale size, and are subject to the risks and whims of satellite launches.

When it comes to Texas data centers, the concerns of tech bros aren’t completely unfounded. Experts tell WIRED that the change in leadership could translate to some concrete changes in the industry—albeit with limits.

Although Democrats have control of the Texas House, Republicans still have control over the state’s senate. Robert Paterson, professor of land use and environmental planning at the University of Texas at Austin, tells WIRED that the split means that some immediate attempts at change “will probably be stymied a bit.”

Adrian Shelley, director of nonprofit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen’s Texas office, tells WIRED that the legislature would be a likely place to hash out high-impact policies like the reallocation of state agency resources. However, he adds that the governor could effect more immediate changes by issuing executive orders, or requesting the resignation of politically appointed officials in state agencies.

Shelley says that these oversight agencies—such as the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, the Public Utility Commission, and the Texas Water Development Board—have the authority to charge fines for breaking state law, or in extreme cases, to revoke permits for projects like data centers. But Paterson notes that Texas developers have particularly strong “vested rights,” which protects the terms of their projects from the moment their permits are approved, even if construction hasn’t begun yet.

Another medium-term route to reshaping Texas's data center industry could be giving more power to its counties. Paterson noted that nearly half of the state’s data centers exist in unincorporated territory, which puts them outside the jurisdiction of city zoning laws.

Unlike other states, Paterson says, Texas counties have relatively limited enforcement abilities. Under the state's so-called Dillon's Rule, counties only have powers that are “specifically allotted to it by the state.” So while they have authority over things like access and egress to county roads, or construction on floodplains, he says they don't have the zoning authority that would help closely regulate projects like data centers.

Paterson says that the new attorney general could theoretically adjust the terms in the state’s biannual handbook, which establishes the limits of county authority. He also argues that even in a split legislature, especially since anti-data center sentiment crosses party lines, state lawmakers could propose a viable bill giving counties “limited zoning authority over data centers."

Shelley tells WIRED that since “data centers were a decisive factor in this blue wave,” the upcoming legislative season will be “very interesting.”

“I will say the data center industry hasn't shown a lot of interest in working with state lawmakers or local leaders,” Shelley says, “and I will be interested to see if that changes.”

If not, there’s always low-Earth orbit.

items.title: Nintendo's biggest ROM chip supplier is bowing out of the business
items.summary: And what that could mean for physical Switch game costs.
items.content:
For years, the AI industry’s insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM , SSDs , and GPUs . Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges.

Chip manufacturer Macronix announced in its third-quarter earnings report that the company’s production of ROM chips “has reached its end” and that it will begin “gradually decoupling from the game industry,” as reported by Taiwanese news site BigGo Finance . That could be an issue for Nintendo, which analyst David Gibson notes uses Macronix as its “main memory chip maker” for physical game cartridges.

That ROM production—which has shrunk 39 percent in the last year and now represents just 5 percent of Macronix’s business—is being crowded out by production of more lucrative, in-demand chips like NOR- and NAND-based memory and eMMCs, the company said. With Macronix’s production capacity stuck at 25,000 12-inch wafers a month—and $1.2 billion in planned new capacity taking a year or more to spin up—less profitable ROM chips are taking up wafer space that can earn more through other types of chips.

This doesn’t mean Nintendo will follow Sony into a world without physical game production . On the contrary, the Switch maker said last month that it had no plans to give up on the game cartridges in the near future. But those cartridges could get more expensive to produce as Nintendo is forced to rely on suppliers like Rohm and Lapis Semiconductor for its remaining ROM chips.

That could have a knock-on effect on the prices publishers charge for physical Switch cartridges, too. Earlier this year, Nintendo started charging more for some physical games than for the equivalent digital download. And last year , Japanese publisher Inin only committed to a full Switch cartridge release for R-Type Dimensions III after it said “two new smaller cartridge [storage capacity] sizes for Nintendo Switch 2” lowered the cost of producing those carts.

On the other hand, Gibson notes that digital software sales represented 61.5 percent of Nintendo’s business in the second calendar quarter of 2026, up slightly from the year before. If that number keeps increasing, lower demand for ROM-based Nintendo cartridges could end up balancing out the costs involved in due time.

items.title: AI PACs spent millions trying to shape Congress — here’s how they fared
items.summary: AI industry PACs spent millions influencing the 2026 midterms, with mixed results. Political groups are already looking toward the next election cycle.
items.content:
Political groups both supporting and opposing the AI industry spent millions of dollars trying to influence Tuesday’s midterm elections and shape the future of AI regulation. That spending produced mixed results, with some of the most heavily backed candidates losing their races.

On the industry side, two AI-focused political action committees (PACs) that raised and spent money to influence the elections — American Mission and Building the Future — collectively spent $4.8 million to back South Carolina Senate candidate Darline Graham, who lost. American Mission is the Republican spending arm of Leading the Future (LTF), a broader political group backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and the VC firm Andreessen Horowitz.

American Mission also spent more than $500,000 apiece supporting Republican House candidates Aaron Flint in Montana and Laurie Buckhout in North Carolina, both of whom lost. LTF’s Democratic spending arm, Think Big, had better luck backing Florida Rep. Jared Moskowitz, who won reelection.

Groups advocating for stronger AI safeguards also saw mixed results. Public First, which is backed by Anthropic, supported several Republicans who lost through its affiliated PAC but had more success backing Democratic candidates. It also contributed $3 million to a PAC supporting California state Sen. Scott Wiener, who was leading his race at the time of publication.

Meanwhile, Guardrails Alliance , a group that has sought to make taking money from AI companies a political liability, spent more than $1 million apiece opposing two candidates who lost: California Rep. Jimmy Gomez and Montana’s Aaron Flint. It also spent $300,000 supporting Angela Gonzales-Torres, who defeated Gomez.

It’s difficult to separate the impact of AI-related spending from the broader Democratic wave that swept Tuesday’s elections. Elon Musk, who reportedly poured half a billion dollars into supporting Republicans in the midterms, also saw many of his candidates lose . Indeed, LTF also backed some candidates it believed were likely to win, only to see them lose to the Dems.

For LTF, though, the general election wasn’t the main focus. The group told TechCrunch ahead of Election Day that it thinks primaries (the contests that choose each party’s nominee) are a more effective use of its money, because spending there can build name recognition and help candidates set up AI policy agendas.

LTF spent $27.38 million in the primaries, including $8 million alone on opposing New York Assembly member Alex Bores , who lost his bid for Congress back in June. When deciding whether it’s worth jumping into a general election race, LTF assesses how competitive the race is, whether it thinks spending could make a difference, and whether it should keep its powder dry for future elections.

Charlie Blaettler, political director of Guardrails Alliance, had a different theory for why LTF spent comparatively little in the general election.

“They don’t want their money to become an issue in these elections,” he said. He pointed to the Michigan Senate primary election, in which a pro-Israel lobbying group called AIPAC spent close to $30 million backing Democratic candidate Haley Stevens against Abdul El-Sayed. Stevens conceded the primary to El-Sayed, who went on to win the Senate seat.

“AIPAC became the story in that race,” Blaettler said. “We know people hate AI billionaires. They hate the people running these companies. They’re very distrustful and disgusted by the political spending and lobbying that the tech industry does. If they spend in a competitive race, they would just become an enormous liability for their candidates.”

The main fight among AIPACs, whether they are pro-industry or pro-regulation, is whether Congress should establish a national AI framework that overrides state laws , or whether states will maintain their own ability to impose safeguards.

Neither side seems poised to back down. LTF, which favors a single national AI framework, told TechCrunch it plans to keep spending in the 2028 elections, while Guardrails Alliance says it wants to keep opposing candidates backed by the AI industry.

Blaettler said that while LTF’s ads rarely touch on AI, instead focusing on popular issues for each candidate, Guardrail Alliance’s ads are specifically about who is taking money from the AI industry.

“Our goal is to make AI money politically toxic,” Blaettler said.

items.title: Qualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sink
items.summary: With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with comp
items.content:
Qualcomm expects data center chips will eventually account for 30% of its business.

With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with companies like Amazon and Meta announced earlier this year. The company expects that portion of its business to grow quickly, forecasting around $650 million in data center revenue during the first quarter of 2027. But it anticipates that will reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and $15 billion by 2029.

Considering the company’s total revenue for 2026 was $10.4 billion, that would constitute a significant share of its earnings. It confirmed during the call that it expects data centers to eventually account for around 30 percent of its business.

That’s not quite as ambitious as AMD, which says that it expects over 80 percent of its revenue will eventually come from data centers. But it suggests there’s plenty of demand that needs to be filled and enough AI money to go around.

items.title: Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones
items.summary: Researchers say group may have been Kremlin-sponsored in search of diplomatic targets.
items.content:
Hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin exploited previously patched iOS and Android flaws in an attempt to hack visitors of multiple websites, including one celebrating the 250th anniversary of the signing of the US Constitution, researchers said Wednesday.

One of the impersonated sites was america250.org, belonging to a non-partisan group of lawmakers, business executives, and at least one former member of the Trump administration. The attackers registered america250[.]holiday and used it as a reverse proxy to america250.org. The imposter website delivered content from the real one that added malicious JavaScript into it.

“We assess that the intrusion set may have deliberately selected this website due to its association with a high-profile national celebration, potentially leveraging the event as a pretext for invitation-themed spear-phishing campaigns,” researchers from security firm Sekoia said .

A second website, theowo[.]club, proxied the website Raffles of London OWO, a luxury hotel physically close to some of the UK’s most sensitive government institutions, including the Ministry of Defence and 10 Downing Street, the official residence and office of the British Prime Minister. Open source reporting indicates that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stayed there during a visit on October 14.

“By doing this watering hole [impersonating] the Raffles London at The OWO, the intrusion set may have sought to target diplomatic delegations and high-profile guests through targeted spear-phishing campaigns,” the researchers said.

The attackers also delivered their attacks through compromised websites—including a top Ukrainian gas production company—and a Ukrainian web analytics service that serves thousands of websites. Sekoia said its attribution to the Kremlin is based on the targets’ profiles and similarities to a previous attack attributed to APT29, one of the names the suspected Russian group is tracked under.

The hackers relied on three infection vectors: direct JavaScript injection into traffic from legitimate websites, proxy domains such as america250[.]holiday, and the supply-chain compromise of the Ukrainian web analytics service. In each case, the injected JavaScript was the same. During the first stage, the JavaScript profiled the visitor’s browser and device. The attackers then used that information to deliver one of three zero-click exploit chains, which work without requiring any interaction from the target.

One of the chains was DarkSword, an iOS exploit kit that Google researchers said customers of PARS Defense, a commercial surveillance vendor in Turkey, and at least two other threat actors have used. Sekoia said the more recent campaign used two other exploit chains that weren’t named.

All of the vulnerabilities exploited in the campaign were “n-days,” meaning they had already been patched and attacks worked only on outdated versions of iOS or Android.

items.title: Nothing CEO says company’s mysterious AI-first device is dropping next month
items.summary: While it's not yet clear what kind of product the smartphone startup is cooking up, Nothing's CEO said the product is designed to leverage AI for productivity gains.
items.content:
Nothing, the smartphone startup behind the distinctive Nothing Phone , is working on an AI product, but what it is remains unclear.

On Wednesday, CEO Carl Pei posted on X that the company’s first “AI-native product” ships in December. “It’s a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product. It has no new screen, and it couldn’t have been an app,” Pei wrote.

Pei has teased an AI-first device for some time and the company has also said that it plans to release a pair of AI-linked smart glasses, as well as earbuds with AI integrations.

Pei’s description adds up to a screenless non-app that uses AI? He also calls it a “productivity tool.” Adding further mystique to the announcement, Pei seems to downplay any link to AI wearables.

“The whole industry is hunting for its iPhone moment: the pendant, the pin, the glasses, the companion, some magical consumer device that makes AI part of everyone’s life,” Pei wrote. “I admire the boldness, but I read this moment differently.”

No firm release date has been announced, but Nothing fans should know soon enough what the company has in store for them.

한국전력(사장 김동철)은 강원본부 신축 사옥이 연면적 1만 5000㎡ 이상 국내 업무시설로는 처음으로 제로에너지건축물(ZEB) 1등급 예비인증을 획득했다고 4일 밝혔다.

강원본부 신축 사옥은 강원도 춘천시 후평동에 연면적 1만 6471㎡ 규모로 올해 12월 착공해 2029년 준공을 목표로 진행하고 있다.

한전에 따르면 강원본부 신축 사옥은 애초 ZEB 3등급 예비인증을 획득했으나 다양한 에너지 기술을 적용해 ZEB 1등급으로 상향했다.

한전 관계자는 “정부가 2050년까지 모든 공공건물에 ZEB 1등급을 의무화한 목표보다 25년 앞서 추진하는 것”이라며 “공공부문 탄소중립을 선도하는 사례”라고 설명했다.

강원본부 신축 사옥은 에너지자립률 100% 이상 달성을 위해 건축물 에너지 효율을 높이고 재생에너지 설비를 대폭 확대했다. 특히, 태양광 발전설비 용량을 애초 491kW에서 805kW로 늘리고, 태양광 모듈 효율을 20.6%에서 23.1%로 높여 에너지자립률을 기존 약 69%에서 약 106%까지 향상했다.

또 자체 연구개발 중인 유리창호형 페로브스카이트 BIPV, 기존 실리콘셀의 한계 극복을 위해 초고효율 태양광 탠덤셀 등을 시범 도입해 신축 사옥을 미래 에너지 신기술 실증·확산을 위한 테스트베드로 활용하는 등 최첨단 에너지 신기술을 집약할 계획이다.

한전은 강원본부 신축 사옥의 ZEB 1등급 예비인증 획득을 계기로 신축을 추진 중인 경북본부 등 다른 사옥에도 ZEB 1등급으로 상향 적용해 공공건축물 에너지자립과 탄소중립 실현에 앞장설 방침이다.

김동철 한전 사장은 “강원본부 신축 사옥의 ZEB 1등급 추진은 공공기관이 정부 에너지 정책을 선도하는 상징적인 모범 사례가 될 것”이라며 “앞으로도 최고 수준의 제로에너지건축물을 지속해서 건설하고, 에너지 신기술 수준을 한 차원 높이는 마중물 역할로 국가 에너지 산업 발전을 견인하겠다”고 밝혔다.

items.content:
미공개 AI 모델 '페이블 5.5'로 일본 극장판 수준의 2D 애니메이션을 제작했다는 주장 을 3일 소개해 드린 바 있습니다. 개발자는 이미지나 영상 생성 AI를 사용하지 않고 100% 코드만으로 만들었다고 주장했지만, 실제 제작 코드가 공개되지 않아 진위를 둘러싼 논란이 일었습니다.

이처럼 대형언어모델(LLM)이 직접 코드를 작성해 영상을 제작하는 사례는 이미 상당수 등장했습니다. LLM이 글과 코드를 작성하는 데 이어 영상 제작까지 맡기 시작한 것입니다. 최근에는 개발자들의 실험을 넘어 기업 이용자를 위한 제품도 등장했습니다.

글과 코드를 생성하는 LLM이 영상을 만드는 방식은 기존 영상 생성 AI와는 다릅니다. 픽셀을 생성해서 화면을 직접 만들어내는 것이 아니라, 영상을 그리는 프로그램을 작성하는 방식입니다.

예를 들어 화면에 글자가 나타나고 그래프가 커지거나 자동차가 왼쪽에서 오른쪽으로 움직이는 장면은 프로그램 코드로 구현할 수 있습니다. LLM은 이용자의 설명에 따라 이러한 코드를 작성하고, 컴퓨터가 이를 실행해 움직이는 장면을 만듭니다.

여기에 반드시 전용 영상 생성 AI가 필요한 것은 아닙니다. 웹 브라우저에서 그림과 애니메이션을 구현하는 자바스크립트나 HTML 캔버스 같은 기존 기술만으로도 간단한 2D 영상을 만들 수 있습니다. LLM이 글자와 도형을 배치하고 시간에 따라 위치와 크기, 색상이 달라지도록 코드를 작성하는 것입니다. 프로그램이 시간 순서대로 그린 화면을 이어 붙이면 하나의 영상이 완성됩니다.

기존 영상 제작 도구를 이용하는 방법도 있습니다. 대표적인 것이 ' 리모션(Remotion) '입니다. 리모션은 웹 개발 기술을 이용해 영상을 만드는 도구로, 원래는 개발자가 직접 코드를 작성해야 했습니다. 이제는 '클로드 코드'나 '코덱스' 같은 AI 코딩 에이전트가 리모션용 코드를 대신 작성하고, 리모션이 이를 실행해 영상으로 만들어 줍니다.

AI 코딩 에이전트는 코드를 작성하는 데 그치지 않고 실행 결과를 확인해 수정하기도 합니다. 화면에서 글자가 겹치거나 움직임이 어색하면 해당 부분의 코드를 다시 작성하는 식입니다. 이처럼 작업을 반복하면서 영상을 완성할 수 있습니다.

이때 기존 사진이나 음악을 가져와 영상에 넣을 수도 있습니다. 따라서 LLM이 영상 제작 코드를 직접 작성했다고 해서 영상에 들어가는 이미지와 음악까지 모두 코드로 만들었다는 뜻은 아닙니다.

이미 지난 4월에는 클로드 코드와 리모션을 이용해 자연어 지시로 모션그래픽을 만드는 제작법 이 공유됐습니다. 특히 9월22일 '클로드 오퍼스 5.5' 출시 이후에는 광고 스타일 영상부터 3D 장면, 교육용 설명 영상, 음악에 맞춰 움직이는 그래픽까지 다양한 작품이 잇달아 공개됐습니다.

관련 사례를 수집하는 사이트 24fps 는 클로드 오퍼스 5.5로 제작됐다고 표기된 작품 4077개를 확인했습니다. 이는 제작자들이 밝힌 모델명을 기준으로 집계한 수치이며, 실제 제작 코드를 공개한 작품은 약 10%에 불과합니다. 결과물은 많아졌지만 제작 방식까지 확인할 수 있는 사례는 제한적입니다.

이러한 움직임은 실제 제품으로도 이어졌습니다. 앤트로픽은 지난 10월8일 기업용 베타 기능인 ' 클로드 모션(Claude Motion) '을 공개했습니다. 이용자가 보고서나 차트, 제품 설명 등을 입력하면 클로드가 이를 짧은 애니메이션으로 만들어 줍니다. 완성된 영상은 MP4로 저장할 수 있으며, 글자와 숫자, 움직이는 시간 등을 수정할 수도 있습니다.

앤트로픽은 클로드 모션에 전용 영상 생성 모델을 사용하지 않는다고 밝혔습니다. 클로드가 텍스트와 도형, 차트, 이미지 등을 움직이는 코드를 작성하는 방식입니다. 실사 영화나 복잡한 인물 영상을 만드는 대신 보고서와 데이터를 이해하기 쉬운 그래픽으로 표현하는 데 초점을 맞췄습니다.

이 방식은 수정과 재현이 쉽다는 장점이 있습니다. 예를 들어 매출 증가율이 15%에서 18%로 바뀌면 코드에 입력된 수치를 변경해 그래프와 문구를 수정할 수 있습니다. 화면 전환 시간이나 움직이는 방향도 조정할 수 있습니다. 기존 영상 생성 AI로 만든 장면을 수정하려면 다시 생성해야 할 때가 많지만, 코드 기반 영상은 필요한 부분을 직접 변경할 수 있다는 차이가 있습니다.

물론 모든 영상을 이런 방식으로 만들 수 있는 것은 아닙니다. 복잡한 인물의 움직임이나 사실적인 자연 풍경은 전용 영상 생성 AI가 유리합니다. 온라인에서 화제가 된 일부 애니메이션도 한 줄의 명령만으로 완성된 것처럼 알려졌지만, 실제로는 상세한 지시와 수시간의 코드 작성, 실행, 수정 작업이 필요한 사례가 있었습니다.

영상 제작을 위해 사람이 직접 작성해야 했던 복잡한 프로그램을 이제 LLM이 상당 부분 대신 작성할 수 있게 됐습니다. 기존 영상 생성 AI가 화면을 직접 만들어내는 기술을 발전시켰다면, 클로드와 같은 LLM은 영상 제작 과정 자체를 자동화하는 도구로 발전하고 있습니다.

특히 뉴스와 광고, 데이터 시각화처럼 내용이 자주 바뀌는 분야에서는 수치나 문구를 수정해 영상을 다시 제작할 수 있어 제작 시간과 비용을 줄이는 데 도움이 될 것으로 보입니다.

■ 뤼튼·스캐터랩 양분한 AI 캐릭터챗 시장에 게임사 가세…경쟁 본격화

AI 캐릭터챗이 인기를 끌면서 새로운 수익원을 찾는 게임사들도 시장에 뛰어들고 있습니다. 캐릭터 IP와 콘텐츠 수익화에 강점을 가진 게임사들의 진출이 시장 경쟁을 어떻게 바꿔놓을지 관심이 모입니다.

■ 오픈AI, 12월부터 챗GPT·코덱스 사용량 통합…기존 앱 1월 종료

오픈AI가 예고한 대로 챗GPT의 '챗'과 '워크'를 하나로 합치는 데 이어, 12월부터 챗GPT와 코덱스의 사용량 한도도 통합합니다. 그동안 다양한 AI 모델과 앱, 기능을 잇달아 선보였던 오픈AI가 이제는 이용자 편의성을 높이기 위해 서비스와 사용 체계를 통합하고 있습니다.

■ 르쿤, 다른 AI가 같은 세상 이해하는 조건 증명…학습 샘플 42배 절감

얀 르쿤이 사진과 글처럼 서로 다른 데이터를 학습한 AI들이 비슷한 방식으로 세상을 이해하게 되는 조건을 수학적으로 제시했습니다. 특히 'JEPA' 학습 방식을 적용하면 기존 언어모델의 다음 토큰 예측 방식보다 42배 적은 학습 샘플로 같은 수준의 내부 표현 유사성을 확보할 수 있다고 밝혔습니다.

items.title: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says
items.summary: During its busiest week last quarter, Uber said only four people booked a ride using an AI agent.
items.content:
Very few people are using personal AI agents to order Ubers, apparently. On the transportation giant’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, the company said that only four rides were ordered through an AI agent during its busiest week in October: the week of Halloween.

While more people used an AI agent to order food through its delivery service, Uber Eats, the volume was still fairly small compared to the overall number of trips.

Uber’s chief financial officer, Balaji Krishnamurthy, told Wall Street analysts on the call that the company handled around 320 million trips and orders across Uber and Uber Eats during the week of Halloween, but only 500 Uber Eats orders were placed by an AI agent.

“It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far,” said CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, referring to the low number of orders placed by AI agents. “Listen, we hope that there will be more traction.”

The surprisingly low numbers of AI-initiated transactions come amid growing hype for a new wave of AI agents that don’t just answer questions but also handle tasks on users’ behalf. There’s been an explosion of personal AI startups, including one of the buzziest, Instinct, which was founded last year and raised its most recent round of funding at a $10 billion valuation. Meta’s Muse also became the No. 1 app in Apple’s U.S. App Store last month, topping 10 million users, per Meta’s own reporting . The company said many were using it to shop and transact with businesses.

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceXAI (Grok) are also now offering their own AI agents, as are numerous smaller startups.

Still, early numbers from public companies indicate the agentic web still has a long way to go. DoorDash, for instance, said last week on its earnings call that it has only received a few hundred orders from AI agents so far, as most customers are still placing orders through the DoorDash app.

Uber is seeing the same behavior, it seems. Khosrowshahi pointed out that the average time to book a ride is only 50 seconds in the company’s app, and re-ordering a favorite food only takes 90 seconds. That suggests an AI agent isn’t necessarily saving anyone time.

Despite the low number of AI-driven transactions, Khosrowshahi seemed bullish on the idea of agents in general. “We think that is another opportunity to reach our platform. We think it will be a net positive in terms of demand on the ecosystem,” he said.

Right now, there are around eight major AI assistants on the market, Khosrowshahi noted, and he expects that number to grow to more than 10 in time.

“Every single AI system company is talking to us,” he added.

items.title: Snapchat surpasses 30M paid subscribers
items.summary: The milestone comes a year after Snapchat announced a controversial limit on free storage for its Memories feature and informed users it would start requiring users to pay $1.99 per month for additional storage or subscribe to Snapchat+ to retain their Memories.
items.content:
As for the company’s broader earnings release, Snap’s shares fell 12% after missing ad revenue and user growth estimates.

Snap reported 495 million daily active users for the quarter, up from 493 million in the previous quarter. However, the figure fell short of analysts’ expectations of 499 million.

“Daily engagement has historically been stable as a percentage of monthly engagement, but we do not intend to optimize Snapchat around daily use at the expense of long-term value for our community,” the investor letter said. “A longer-term horizon better aligns our reported metrics with the product and safety decisions that strengthen relationships, create lasting utility, and support broader, more durable audience growth.”

Spiegel said in the letter than while advertising revenue growth remains below the company’s target, the company plans to prioritize improving advertiser performance and expanding the ways businesses can reach its users.

items.title: AMD's record quarter: Data center business doubles, while gaming craters
items.summary: AMD's gaming revenue fell 40 percent in an otherwise record $13.4 billion quarter.
items.content:
AMD reported third-quarter revenues on Tuesday with a record $13.4 billion, an increase of 45 percent year over year, as data center business nearly doubled and the company’s gaming segment cratered.

AMD CFO Jean Hu said, “We expect revenue to be approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3%. The middle point of our guidance represents approximately 66% year-over-year revenue growth, primarily driven by the acceleration of our Data Center segment.” AMD says its Q4 revenue projections are up another 27 percent from this quarter’s results. As reported by Tom’s Hardware , Intel’s Q4 guidance places revenue estimates between $15 and $16 billion. That means that if both companies land where they expect to at the end of the fourth quarter, AMD would exceed Intel’s revenue for the first time in history.

The data center segment of AMD’s business was up 97 percent year over year, with a record $8.5 billion. AMD attributes the growth to demand for its EPYC line of enterprise server CPUs, along with the launch of the Instinct MI450 series GPUs . Sales of AMD Ryzen mobile chips led growth in the Client business, which includes desktop Ryzen processors and posted $2.95 billion in revenue, up 7 percent year over year.

Gaming revenue fell sharply for the company, posting a 40 percent drop in revenue at $773 million, which AMD attributes to “lower semi-custom and graphics revenue.” Operating margins in AMD’s data center business expanded from 25 percent to 34 percent, with operating income surging 168 percent to $2.88 billion.

Credit: AMD Credit: AMD

Embedded segment revenue, or all the SoCs , FPGAs , and boards under AMD’s umbrella that go into other hardware, was $1.1 billion, up 29 percent. AMD attributed this growth to gains made in the “aerospace and defense, automotive, communications, and industrial end markets.”

The gaming segment of AMD’s business is composed of two main sources. There are semi-custom processors that AMD supplies to other manufacturers’ consoles, as well as its own Radeon graphics business. Where things can get confusing is that Ryzen processors, like those commonly installed in gaming PCs, are counted under the company’s client business, not gaming. According to AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su , “In Gaming, revenue declined 40% year over year to $773 million, primarily due to lower semi-custom sales as expected at this stage of the console cycle.” The financial results do not break down the split between console chip sales and PC graphics cards.

Along with the Q3 financial results, AMD used the occasion to highlight hardware still in the hopper. The new AMD Threadripper Halo Station , which AMD first showed at IFA in September , pairs a Threadripper 9995WX CPU with up to four Instinct MI350P GPUs and can run trillion-parameter LLMs locally. The system is slated for a release sometime in 2027, with pricing still to be announced.

AMD also announced that Windows-based systems running on its Ryzen AI Halo platform will be “coming soon.” Known as Project Zenith , the effort will support a developer-focused Windows experience on the current PRO 400 Series platform . Built on the Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 processor , the chip supports up to 192GB of unified system memory, with up to 160GB of that available to be allocated for graphics, and is capable of running 300 billion-parameter models at 4-bit quantization. On the call, Su stated that AMD “started shipping MI455X in volume in the quarter, and lead customers, including Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Oracle, brought their first Helios racks online quickly.”

items.title: OpenAI is already trying to shape the 2028 election
items.summary: OpenAI’s Chris Lehane wants AI to define the 2028 election, proposing a new social contract that could benefit Americans while also advancing the AI giant’s own business interests.
items.content:
OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane thinks the 2028 presidential election could be a defining moment for AI. And he wants politicians to start developing policies that address Americans’ concerns about the technology, rather than simply paying lip service to anti-AI sentiment and the backlash against data centers .

In a new essay , Lehane compares AI’s potential to reshape the economy to President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal, the 1930s set of federal programs and reforms enacted after industrialization and the Great Depression shattered the old economic order. He observes that Americans today feel similarly anxious about losing control over their economic futures and urges politicians to find a “compelling third path” that allows people to share in AI’s benefits. He lays out five policy priorities, spanning worker protections and education to AI safety and data center development.

The essay comes on the heels of a stunning Democratic victory in the midterm elections, in which Democrats flipped control of Congress amid widespread voter frustration over the cost of living. Kate Brennan, who leads AI and corporate power policy at the AI Now Institute, told TechCrunch that Lehane’s rhetoric marks a notable shift from OpenAI’s policy agenda last year, which focused on accelerating AI development, reducing regulatory barriers, and expanding infrastructure.

Unsurprisingly, many of Lehane’s proposals would encourage wider AI adoption and support the infrastructure expansion companies like OpenAI need to grow. The original New Deal established protections for workers and placed constraints on corporate power. It’s less clear how Lehane’s vision would hold AI companies accountable for the economic disruption their technology could create.

“Invoking a New Deal metaphor is to invoke state capacity to actually benefit the public,” Brennan said. “This is written by a private company that is trying to advocate for policies for its own benefit. It is ahistorical at best and harmful at worst.”

While AI wasn’t a dominant issue in the midterms, opposition to data centers emerged as a major bipartisan concern in several races in the midterms. And Lehane may be right that AI will become a bigger part of the conversation over the next two years.

Affordability is already shaping up as a key issue for the 2028 election as Americans grapple with inflation, tariffs, and the rising cost of living. AI could become an increasingly large part of that conversation as voters stress about data centers hiking up electricity bills, AI replacing their jobs, and technology’s economic gains flowing only to a handful of wealthy companies.

Lehane acknowledges many of these concerns, but he offers few concrete proposals to prevent AI’s gains from becoming concentrated. Instead, he largely pitches AI as a path to greater prosperity for Americans willing to embrace it.

Take his proposals for the tax code. He suggests incentives for workers to learn AI skills, easier capital access for entrepreneurs, and new approaches to employee ownership and profit-sharing. Those are not the same as binding requirements that would ensure workers share in AI-generated wealth or that companies pay the costs of displacing workers.

“I was struck by how much of this policy is for a future…that is already predicated on mass AI adoption and AI benefiting society, which we have yet to see,” Brennan said. “All of it is predicated on benefiting from AI’s upside.”

Brennan said it would make more sense to see things like a revised corporate tax rate or tax incentives for hiring human beings rather than automating jobs, as well as ways to keep companies from amassing outsize market power.

Lehane’s emphasis on expanding AI’s economic opportunities, rather than limiting potential harms, extends to data centers. He notes concerns about data centers while emphasizing the construction jobs and local tax revenue they could generate. He then warns that politicians who support a data center moratorium could jeopardize America’s lead over China, going so far as to compare that stance to the 2002 vote to authorize the Iraq war.

Lehane also makes child safety and education central to his proposed agenda, stressing the importance of age-appropriate protections and safeguards around AI companions for minors. He also warns against keeping AI out of classrooms , arguing that doing so could lead to inequality between wealthy students and “children in rural communities.” But the argument takes for granted that AI improves learning, a claim that remains unproven and one critics say deserves more examination than more funding or individualized attention from human teachers.

Lehane also calls for enforceable AI safety standards, independent evaluations, public oversight, and the ability to restrict AI systems or use a kill switch to shut them down — though recent studies show that OpenAI and other AI labs haven’t published comprehensive plans for what they would do if a model escaped human control.

Brennan called these stances “disingenuous,” pointing to OpenAI’s history of opposing legislation designed to impose such measures. In 2024, for example, OpenAI opposed California’s AI safety bill, SB 1047, which would have mandated catastrophic risk evaluations and shutdown capabilities. Last year, OpenAI also sought to limit state regulation , arguing that states could undermine American innovation. The company has more recently shifted some of those positions, backing several state safety laws and saying it would be open to independent evaluators embedded in the company.

Lehane also argues that people should maintain control over consequential decisions made using AI, rather than handing off judgment entirely to machines. But that raises the question of what human control really looks like in a society where humans are increasingly being required to use AI in education, work, healthcare, and government.

items.title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
items.summary: The startup allows software engineers to deploy teams of agents to work on various aspects of a project simultaneously.
items.content:
Meta has acquired Conductor , an AI coding startup that allows users to spin up software projects by deploying multiple agents into parallel workspaces.

The news was originally reported by Axios, and Conductor shared news of its acquisition on its blog.

“I have big news: Conductor is joining Meta,” wrote the startup’s founder and CEO, Charlie Holtz, on Wednesday. “We have some big, crazy plans for the next interface,” he added, teasing that the company would have “something new” for customers to use by “early next year.”

On X, Holtz also noted that he was looking forward to working with Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, and Nat Friedman, head of product at the company’s Superintelligence Labs. “They’ve been on an absolute tear, and I’m convinced MSL has the highest talent density of all the labs,” he added.

Meta confirmed the acquisition to TechCrunch but wouldn’t comment further or provide additional details about the deal.

Conductor, founded in 2024, only launched its core product just last summer. The company’s agentic teams, which can be deployed in the cloud, locally, or via a user’s phone, are designed to help software engineers work on separate, compartmentalized parts of a project in concert. The agents that the platform deploys aren’t developed in-house but come from major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI.

Holtz said that, until early next year, Conductor’s core features would continue to work as they previously have. The exception is Conductor’s cloud service, which will shut down on November 20, after which the company will begin deleting user cloud data.

Meta, which previously lagged behind in AI services, has spent the last several months trying to catch up. In August, the company launched Muse Code , its own coding agent. Meanwhile, the company’s recently launched Muse agents are seeing significant adoption, with the company recently reporting that the service had surpassed 10 million users. The company has also made a number of AI-related acquisitions over the past year, including Moltbook , the viral agent platform that made headlines.

items.content:
미국 중간선거에서 민주당이 압승하면서 AI 데이터센터 건설에 제동이 걸릴 가능성이 커졌지만, 아마존과 마이크로소프트(MS) 등 빅테크 주가는 오히려 급등했다. 신규 데이터센터 건설이 늦어지면 막대한 AI 투자 부담이 줄고 기존 시설의 가치가 높아질 것이라는 기대가 나타난 가운데, 차입금으로 데이터센터를 확장해 온 중소형 기업들은 주가가 급락하며 희비가 엇갈렸다.

로이터 등에 따르면, 4일(현지시간) 미국 증시에서 아마존 주가는 장중 7.4% 급등하며 3개월 만에 최고치를 기록했다. 메타와 알파벳, MS도 2~6.3% 상승했다. AI 인프라 투자가 상대적으로 적은 애플은 약 7% 올라 사상 최고치를 기록했다. 상승세가 유지되면 이들 5개 기업의 시가총액이 하루 만에 7500억달러(약 1000조원) 이상 늘어날 것으로 추산됐다.

이번 상승에는 정치적 불확실성 해소도 영향을 미쳤다. 민주당이 상·하원을 모두 장악하면서 트럼프 행정부의 급격한 정책 변화에 제약이 생길 것이라는 기대가 투자심리를 개선했다. 특히 빅테크에는 민주당의 데이터센터 규제 강화 가능성이 오히려 AI 투자 부담을 줄이는 요인으로 평가됐다.

최근 빅테크 주가는 AI 인프라에 투입하는 막대한 자금이 실제 수익으로 이어질 수 있는지를 둘러싼 불안감으로 하락세를 보였다. 주요 빅테크의 올해 자본지출 계획은 총 7400억달러를 넘어 지난해 4000억달러에서 크게 늘었다. 최근 실적 발표에서도 데이터센터와 AI 반도체 투자 증가로 현금흐름이 악화할 수 있다는 지적이 잇따랐다.

그러나 민주당의 승리로 신규 데이터센터 건설 속도가 늦어질 가능성이 커지면서 시장의 평가가 달라졌다. 이미 대규모 데이터센터를 확보한 빅테크는 신규 시설 공급이 제한되면 기존 컴퓨팅 자원의 가치가 높아지고, 신규 시설에 대한 자본지출 증가세도 완만해질 수 있다는 분석이다.

아트 호건 B. 라일리 웰스 수석 시장전략가는 "선거 이후 신규 데이터센터 건설이 다소 느려지거나 장애물을 만날 수 있다"라며 "대형 기술 기업들은 이미 데이터센터를 보유하고 있어 과잉 건설이 줄어들면 기존 자산의 가치가 높아질 것"이라고 설명했다. 또 건설 속도가 완만해지면 기업들의 자본지출 부담도 줄어들 수 있다고 분석했다.

이런 시장 반응은 데이터센터 건설이 이번 중간선거의 주요 쟁점으로 떠오른 것과 관련이 있다. 워싱턴포스트에 따르면 텍사스와 조지아, 오하이오 등 주요 데이터센터 건설 지역에서 신규 시설 제한과 규제 강화를 주장한 민주당 주지사 후보들이 승리했다. 전력과 수자원 소비, 소음, 공공요금 인상 등에 대한 주민들의 불만이 선거 과정에서 중요한 현안으로 등장했다.

특히 미국 데이터센터 건설의 핵심 거점인 텍사스에서는 지나 히노호사 주지사 당선자가 주민 보호 대책이 마련될 때까지 신규 데이터센터 건설을 중단하겠다고 공약했다. 조지아와 오하이오에서도 개발업체의 비용 부담을 높이거나 건설 승인 기준을 강화하겠다는 공약이 나왔다.

지역 주민들이 직접 데이터센터 개발을 제한하는 움직임도 나타났다. 이번 선거에서 미국 최소 38개 지역의 유권자들이 데이터센터 건설을 금지하거나 제한하는 방안을 통과시켰다. 일부 지역에서는 신규 시설 건설을 일정 기간 중단하거나 대규모 전력을 사용하는 시설을 제한하는 조치가 채택됐다. 데이터센터에 대한 반발은 민주당 지지 지역에만 국한되지 않아 양당 모두 관련 정책을 재검토해야 하는 상황이다.

이와 달리 신규 데이터센터 개발에 집중해 온 기업들은 타격을 받았다. 어플라이드디지털과 아이렌의 주가는 이날 장중 6~13% 하락했다. 코어위브와 네비우스 등 AI 클라우드 기업들도 대규모 설비 투자를 진행하고 있어 향후 규제 변화에 민감할 수밖에 없는 상황이다.

이들 기업은 급증하는 AI 컴퓨팅 수요에 대응하기 위해 대규모 차입과 설비 투자를 진행하고 있다. 그러나 신규 데이터센터 건설 승인이 늦어지거나 세제 혜택이 축소되면 투자 비용이 늘고, 고객에게 컴퓨팅 자원을 제공하기까지 걸리는 시간도 길어진다. 기존 시설을 대규모로 보유한 빅테크와 달리 신규 건설에 대한 의존도가 높다는 점이 부담이다.

민주당의 승리가 곧바로 전국적인 데이터센터 건설 제한으로 이어지는 것은 아니다. 도널드 트럼프 대통령이 여전히 행정부를 이끌고 있어 연방 차원의 입법에는 제약이 있으며, 주정부와 지방정부의 인허가 정책이 단기적으로 더 직접적인 영향을 줄 수 있다. 실제로 얼마나 많은 데이터센터 건설 계획이 지연될지도 아직 불확실하다.

빅테크도 장기적으로는 규제 강화의 영향을 받을 수 있다. 아마존과 MS, 구글, 메타도 신규 데이터센터를 통해 AI 컴퓨팅 자원을 늘리고 있어 건설이 지연되면 서비스 확장과 미래 매출 증가에 부담이 생길 수 있기 때문이다. 이번 주가 상승은 데이터센터 규제가 빅테크에 무조건 유리하다는 의미가 아니라, 과도한 AI 투자 경쟁의 속도가 완만해질 가능성을 시장이 긍정적으로 평가한 결과로 풀이된다.

items.content:
외국인 투자 수요 발굴·인허가 애로 해소 협력…투자 가이드북 발간 추진

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/11/05 06:01

한국데이터센터연합회(KDCC)가 대한무역투자진흥공사(코트라)와 손잡고 국내 인공지능(AI) 데이터센터 산업의 외국인 투자 유치 확대에 나선다. 글로벌 투자 네트워크와 국내 데이터센터 산업 전문성을 결합해 해외 투자사와 국내 기업 간 협력을 강화하고 전력 확보와 인허가 등 투자 과정에서 발생하는 어려움을 해소한다는 목표다.

한국데이터센터연합회는 코트라와 지난 4일 서울 파르나스 호텔에서 데이터센터 외국인 투자 유치 협력을 위한 업무협약(MOU)을 체결했다고 5일 밝혔다.

이번 협약은 AI 산업 성장에 따라 데이터센터 인프라 투자 수요가 확대되는 가운데 해외 자본 유치를 통해 국내 AI 데이터센터 구축을 지원하기 위해 마련됐다. 협약식은 '인베스트 코리아 서밋 2026' 부대 행사로 진행됐다.

JP모건에 따르면 전 세계 AI 데이터센터 인프라에는 오는 2030년까지 약 5조 5000억 달러가 투자될 전망이다. AI 모델 개발과 서비스 확대로 고성능 연산 인프라 수요가 증가하면서 데이터센터 구축을 위한 자본 확보도 주요 과제로 떠오르고 있다.

우리 정부도 AI 데이터센터를 반도체, 피지컬 AI와 함께 '대한민국 대도약 3대 메가프로젝트'로 선정하고 대규모 투자 확대를 추진 중이다. 민간에서 합동으로 550조원을 투자해 총 8.4기가와트(GW) 규모 AI 데이터센터를 구축하고 정부는 이를 지원하며 전후방 산업 생태계를 육성한다는 구상이다.

인허가 일괄 처리와 비수도권 전력 공급 특례 등을 담은 '인공지능 데이터센터 산업 진흥에 관한 특별법'도 내년 3월 시행될 예정이다.

양 기관은 이번 협약을 통해 한국데이터센터연합회의 산업 전문성과 코트라의 글로벌 투자 유치 네트워크를 결합할 계획이다. 해외 투자사와 국내 데이터센터 기업을 연결하고 투자 과정에서 필요한 정보와 지원을 제공하는 협력 체계를 구축한다는 방침이다.

현재 코트라는 전 세계 36개 투자유치 전담무역관을 운영하고 있다. 한국데이터센터연합회에는 데이터센터 운영과 설계·건설, 장비·설비 분야 기업 등 199개 회원사가 참여 중이다.

주요 협력 분야는 ▲데이터센터 외국인 투자 수요 발굴 및 투자 촉진 ▲데이터센터 구축 가이드 발간 ▲해외 투자사와 국내 데이터센터 기업 간 협력 지원 ▲데이터센터 투자 애로 해소 등이다.

특히 해외 투자사가 국내 데이터센터 사업에 참여하는 과정에서 겪는 전력 확보와 인허가 문제 해결에 협력할 계획이다. 양 기관은 앞서 지난달 23일 데이터센터 외국인 투자기업 간담회를 공동 개최해 현장 애로사항과 지원 수요를 파악한 바 있다.

이를 바탕으로 내년 3월 AI 데이터센터 특별법 시행 시점에 맞춰 외국인 투자사가 알아야 할 투자 절차와 관련 제도를 정리한 가이드북을 발간할 예정이다. 투자 신고와 입지 선정 등 사업 추진 과정에서 발생하는 어려움을 줄이기 위한 지원도 이어갈 방침이다.

한국데이터센터연합회와 코트라는 국내 데이터센터 산업계와 글로벌 투자사 간 협력 기회를 확대해 AI 인프라 구축에 필요한 해외 자본 유입을 촉진한다는 목표다.

강중협 한국데이터센터연합회장은 "AI 데이터센터 적기 구축과 국내 데이터센터 산업에 글로벌 표준을 도입하기 위해선 적극적인 해외 투자 유치가 필요하다"며 "해외 투자유치 조직망, 노하우를 가진 코트라와 함께 국내 데이터센터 산업계와 글로벌 기업을 연결하는 창구 역할을 수행해 데이터센터 산업에 외국인 투자유치 효과를 높이기 위해 최선을 다하겠다"고 말했다.

items.title: Big Tech claims voters’ AI backlash is “anti-Trump” not “anti-tech”
items.summary: Tech industry in denial as US overwhelmingly votes to restrict AI, data centers.
items.content:
Donald Trump’s big, rapid American AI buildout now faces a major slowdown as voters in yesterday’s elections overwhelmingly supported candidates and measures that favored increasing restrictions on AI and data centers nationwide.

One resource from a polling firm, called Redbud Consulting, tracked data center initiatives on the ballot and reported that out of 44 measures across 10 states seeking to restrict data centers, 38 passed so far. Those measures included dozens of moratoriums and bans. Analysts suggested those won’t impact data centers already under construction or approved through 2027, instead largely impacting future projects planned for 2028. Only one measure passed allowing a data center to proceed. But even that small win represented pushback on the AI industry—requiring data center developers in a North Dakota city to pay for independent reviews and hold public hearings when expanding or proposing projects.

In addition to increasing regulations on data centers, voters also backed anti-AI candidates, electing officials vowing crackdowns in key states building out the most data center capacity in the US.

Most notably, Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor race that Axios reported would fundamentally scramble the math on Trump’s AI buildout. According to Bloomberg , Hinojosa’s election has developers facing down the “worst-case scenario.” Texas is the epicenter of the AI boom, Axios noted, and was expected to account for more than 41 percent of added data center capacity in 2028.

Now, Hinojosa plans to delay projects as long as it takes to pass laws “tackling impacts on water, electricity, air, and property rights.” Approximately “13 gigawatts of data center capacity” is now exposed, Bloomberg reported. Gordon Johnson of GLJ Research warned in a note that Texas projects with “power, permits and steel keep going,” but “those with power but no state environmental permits slip 12 to 18 months,” Bloomberg reported. Some projects may leave the state entirely, perhaps moving to Louisiana or Georgia—or perhaps going nowhere.

“She would impose a moratorium until legislation is passed that gives communities a voice, protects household utility bills, and ends the tax incentives for data centers,” Johnson’s note said. “The question now is how long the pause lasts.” As PIMCO head of public policy Libby Cantrill similarly warned, “even if statewide moratoria do not result, we expect to see a lot more sand in the gears of the AI buildout regardless—with more time required to secure permits and other approvals, as well as more concessions that data center developers will have to make.”

Texas wasn’t the only big shake-up. Democrats won governor races in the next three biggest states previously wooing data center developers—Arizona, Georgia, and Ohio. Overall, Axios projected that “nearly two-thirds of 2028 data center capacity” could face similar delays as Hinojosa threatens in Texas. Bloomberg estimated that half the data centers in the US are now more vulnerable to scrutiny.

For AI firms, that’s a nightmare, since any delays will set back revenue, and IT consulting firm Gartner recently estimated “the AI boom is nearly $5 trillion short of paying for itself.”

Likely soon, developers nationwide will face tighter rules limiting tax incentives and requiring stronger protections for residents around who pays for grid infrastructure and water use. Those kinds of regulations will most likely increase developers’ costs at an inconvenient time, Bloomberg’s report said.

While many reports suggested that the first so-called “AI election” proved the power of the people to rein in Big Tech, some AI industry insiders downplayed the election results on Wednesday. In a statement, Adam Kovacevich—a former Google executive and the CEO of a tech industry trade group and policy coalition called Chamber of Progress—suggested “the results offer little evidence of a voter mandate to crack down on AI or data centers.” He emphasized that “Democratic gubernatorial candidates who opposed data center bans won at a higher rate than those who supported them,” and admonished, “Let’s not confuse an anti-Trump wave with an anti-tech mandate.”

“Voters wanted change on the economy, not a crackdown on innovation,” Kovacevich said, while sharing a resource for those in the tech industry seeking an alternative spin on the results.

NBC News exit polls suggest it’s true that issues like cost of living or government corruption were ranked as more significant by voters than AI and data centers. However, like many analysts who point to AI opposition as a make-or-break issue for many voters, Alejandra Montoya-Boyer, vice president of The Leadership Conference’s Center for Civil Rights and Technology, disagreed with Kovacevich’s lens.

“The 2026 midterms have been the first true AI election in the US,” Montoya-Boyer said. “We saw voters turn up at the polls in record midterm numbers and vote for leaders who are willing to protect them and their rights from unchecked AI.”

Montoya-Boyer cited NBC’s polls showing that 3 in 4 voters are opposed to data centers. Additionally, more than half of voters said that “AI and data centers were a crucial or major factor in their vote for Congress.” The mass backlash is not just about utility costs or other data center fears, Montoya-Boyer suggested, but instead stemmed from a call from voters to regulate AI. Election day came “as the biggest AI companies raced to go public, AI systems broke out of the test ‘sandboxes’ meant to contain them, and biased and discriminatory AI kept making life-altering decisions about us,” Montoya-Boyer said.

“These results confirm numerous polls and what we civil rights leaders have been hearing from the communities we represent: Innovation is only real when it includes all of us and actually improves our lives,” Montoya-Boyer said.

일론 머스크 CEO가 미국 중간선거의 최대 패자 중 한 명으로 꼽혔다. 공화당 승리를 위해 약 5억달러(약 6700억원)를 투입했지만 민주당이 상·하원을 장악하고 핵심 사업 거점인 텍사스에서도 승리하면서, AI 데이터센터 건설과 우주사업 확장, 정부 계약 등에 차질이 생길 수 있다는 전망이 나오고 있다.

로이터와 워싱턴포스트 등 주요 외신은 4일(현지시간) 머스크 CEO가 막대한 정치자금을 투입하고도 공화당의 패배를 막지 못했으며, 그 여파가 기업 경영으로 이어질 수 있다고 보도했다. 특히 그를 이번 중간선거에서 가장 큰 손실을 본 인물 중 한 명으로 평가했다.

머스크는 공화당 후보와 정치단체에 4억달러 이상을 지원하며 최대 개인 정치 후원자로 활동했다. 그러나 민주당은 상·하원 다수당을 차지했으며, 공화당의 오랜 텃밭인 텍사스에서도 지나 히노호사가 그레그 애벗 주지사를 꺾었다. 연방 상원의원 선거에서도 민주당 제임스 탈라리코가 머스크가 지원한 켄 팩스턴을 물리쳤다.

막대한 정치자금이 오히려 역효과를 냈다는 분석도 나왔다. 와이어드가 4일 오전까지 집계한 결과, 머스크의 정치단체 '아메리카 PAC'이 지원한 후보들은 승패가 확정된 21개 선거에서 1승 20패를 기록했다. 탈라리코 당선자는 선거 과정에서 머스크가 막대한 자금으로 정치적 영향력을 확보하려 한다고 비판하며 이를 주요 선거 쟁점으로 활용했다.

무엇보다 텍사스의 패배가 뼈아프다는 평이다. 텍사스는 테슬라와 스페이스X의 본사가 있고, 머스크가 AI 데이터센터와 반도체 생산시설, 자율주행차 사업 등에 대규모 투자를 추진하는 핵심 거점이다. 이곳에서만 2억2400만달러를 공화당에 지원했지만, 주요 선거에서 모두 패했다.

이에 따라 공화당 주정부 아래에서 누려왔던 우호적인 사업 환경에도 변화가 예상된다. 와이어드는 애벗 주지사실이 관할해 온 16억달러 이상의 기업 세제 혜택을 거론하며, 정권 교체가 머스크의 사업에 영향을 줄 수 있다고 분석했다. 향후 신규 투자에 대한 세제 혜택과 인허가 정책이 어떻게 달라질지가 관건이다.

가장 직접적인 사업 위험은 AI 데이터센터 건설이다. 히노호사 당선인은 선거 과정에서 주민 보호 대책이 마련될 때까지 신규 데이터센터 건설을 중단하고 관련 세제 혜택도 폐지해야 한다고 주장했다. 데이터센터의 막대한 전력과 수자원 소비가 주민들의 공공요금 부담을 높인다는 이유다.

이는 AI 컴퓨팅 인프라를 공격적으로 증설해 온 머스크의 계획과 충돌한다. 스페이스X는 테네시주 멤피스 인근의 초대형 AI 데이터센터 '콜로서스'와 '콜로서스 II'를 중심으로 AI 사업을 확대하고 있다. 앤트로픽 등 외부 고객에게 컴퓨팅 자원을 임대하며 매출을 늘렸고, 이 사업은 상장 이후 첫 흑자를 기록하는 데도 기여했다.

스페이스X는 지난 9월 말 1.7기가와트(GW)였던 AI 컴퓨팅 설비 용량을 내년에는 13GW까지 확대한다는 목표를 제시했다. 텍사스 스타베이스에도 신규 컴퓨팅 시설을 계획하고 있어 현지 데이터센터 규제가 강화되면 건설 일정과 투자 비용에 영향받을 수 있다.

스페이스X의 우주사업에도 새로운 변수가 생겼다. 히노호사는 앞서 머스크와 애벗 주지사 사이에 오간 이메일 공개를 요구하는 소송을 제기했으며, 스페이스X의 사업 확장을 위해 해안가 주립공원 부지를 매각하는 방안에도 반대했다. 이에 따라 스타베이스의 토지 확보와 시설 확장 과정에서 주정부와 갈등이 발생할 가능성이 있다.

연방 차원에서도 민주당의 의회 장악으로 머스크 기업에 대한 조사가 강화될 전망이다. 민주당 의원들은 그동안 스페이스X의 정부 계약과 보조금, 우크라이나군의 스타링크 위성통신 이용 제한, 정부효율부(DOGE)에서 추진한 연방 공무원 감축 등을 문제 삼아 왔다. 차기 하원 감독위원장을 맡을 로버트 가르시아 의원도 공화당과 관련 인사들에게 법적 대응을 준비하라는 메시지를 내놓았다.

금융시장에서도 정치적 위험을 반영하는 움직임이 나타났다. 4일 장중 스페이스X와 테슬라 주가는 각각 한때 5.5%, 5.1% 하락하며 주요 주가지수의 상승세와 대조를 이뤘다. 결국 3.3%, 3.8% 하락으로 장을 마감하며 하루 동안 두 회사의 시가총액 약 1300억달러(약 174조원)가 증발했다.

하지만 도널드 트럼프 대통령은 여전히 행정부를 이끌고 있으며, 스페이스X의 우주 발사와 위성통신 사업은 미국의 국가안보 및 우주개발 정책과 긴밀하게 연결돼 있다. 의회의 감독 강화가 실제 계약 축소나 사업 중단으로 이어질지는 불확실하다.

머스크는 선거 결과가 나온 뒤 X에 "이제 우주 데이터센터가 꽤 매력적으로 보인다"라는 글을 게시했다. 지상 데이터센터 규제에 대한 반응으로 해석되지만, 우주 데이터센터는 냉각과 유지보수 등 해결해야 할 기술적 과제가 많다.

막대한 정치자금으로 공화당을 지원했던 그는 앞으로 민주당이 장악한 의회와 텍사스 주정부를 상대로 대규모 투자 계획을 추진해야 하는 상황을 맞았다는 평이다.

items.title: Residential proxies detected on White House network
items.summary: Article URL: https://layer3intel.com/blog/residential-proxies-white-house-network Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50371246 Points: 484 # Comments: 141
items.content:
Our Residential Proxy Observatory , launched earlier this week, is a first-of-its-kind interface that gives researchers a global view of residential proxy and anonymized internet activity.

While our team was looking through it, we noticed residential proxy exit activity on AS2650 . AS2650 is registered to the Executive Office of the President, the federal agency that hosts the White House network. Residential proxy services sell access to everyday devices, letting customers send traffic through them so it appears to come from that device's network.

From October 5 to November 3:

To make sure this was not a fluke, we checked these addresses against other residential proxy detection services, such as Spur and Synthient. Their public IP context pages independently identify these addresses as residential proxy exits.

This is public access. Anybody can obtain it by signing up to a public residential proxy service, paying a few dollars and sending requests through it. We did not selectively target this network or try to make our probes exit from it. We caught this by chance, simply by requesting global rotating access through these services.

Most of the activity happens in the evening, Eastern time: about half of it falls between 5 p.m. and midnight, and almost none happens in the early morning. That pattern suggests a person rather than a public guest Wi-Fi network: someone regularly on the White House network late into the evening, whose device is infected with a proxy SDK. Our data shows the exits, not the device or the person behind them.

Past research has shown that poorly secured proxy SDKs can allow internal network access and lateral movement. This is how past botnets have spread. In A Broken System Fueling Botnets , the researchers at Synthient documented how the Kimwolf botnet reached at least 2 million devices, mostly Android devices with an exposed ADB service, through residential proxy networks. If an SDK on this network has the same kind of flaw, anyone buying proxy access could use it to reach internal systems.

The White House is not the only surprise in the observatory. Residential proxies also reach some of the most isolated places on the planet.

Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha is the South Atlantic territory that includes the most remote inhabited island in the world. We recorded 413 addresses and more than 32,000 observations there, split between Starlink and the island's local internet provider, Sure Saint Helena.

We also recorded three observations from Antarctica . All of them come from a Cloudflare WARP address that points to McMurdo Station.

Other remote places with activity:

Residential proxies have infected every corner of the world, and it looks like there is no place they cannot reach. Layer3 Intel tracks residential proxy and anonymization infrastructure worldwide. Even when the proxies hide in networks on the farthest corners of the planet, we can still observe them, leaving threat actors no place to hide.

items.title: The Biggest Pro-AI Super PAC Network Didn’t Really Impact the Midterms
items.summary: Leading the Future, backed by Silicon Valley’s biggest billionaires, had a war chest of $100 million and an aggressive stance against AI regulation. All of it didn’t add up to much on Tuesday night.
items.content:
Leading the Future, the biggest pro-AI super PAC network , is walking away from the midterm elections with just over $20 million still in the bank and a roster of dozens of successful congressional candidates from both sides of the aisle.

At first glance, that looks like a win. The details tell another story, though. The donations went overwhelmingly to safe candidates, and the results in the small handful of riskier races that Leading the Future got involved with indicate that its plans to shape the election fell flat.

When Leading the Future entered the scene in August 2025 vowing to “ oppose policies that stifle innovation ," it had a war chest of around $100 million thanks to some of Silicon Valley’s biggest tech billionaires—including Andreessen Horowitz, Palantir cofounder Joe Lonsdale , and OpenAI’s Greg Brockman —and was led by major political strategists.

Designed as a “ structured ecosystem ,” it set a goal of having ”maximum flexibility to engage in the 2026 election cycle and beyond.” The network is made up of 501(c)(4) organizations and federal and state super PACs catering to both sides of the aisle: American Mission largely gives to Republicans, while Think Big largely gives to Democrats. Its structure and overlapping strategists quickly drew comparisons to Fairshake, a massive, well-funded pro-crypto super PAC network that dominated in the 2024 election.

“They came out guns a-blazing, saying, ‘Be afraid, we are going to spend our millions to influence not only how lawmakers legislate us but also against you in your primaries and in your reelection,’” Sacha Haworth, executive director of the Tech Oversight Project, tells WIRED. ”The purpose of that was to bully lawmakers into acquiescence, intimidate them into not sticking their necks out on AI safety or tech industry regulation at all.”

Leading the Future did not respond to requests for comment.

Late last year, Leading the Future took on Democrat Alex Bores , a former Palantir engineer and state lawmaker running in New York’s 12th congressional district on an AI safety platform, spending millions of dollars in attack ads against his primary bid.

“They fully expected to bury him, put his head on a spike, and parade it around as proof that they could,” says Haworth. Instead, Bores’ candidacy became a high-profile proxy war between competing AI philosophies, boosting his profile and platform. The pro-AI safety network Public First, which has significant financial backing from Anthropic, spent $15 million boosting Bores’ candidacy. Though Bores didn’t win, he came second in a crowded primary field to another candidate, Micah Lasher, who campaigned on tech accountability and AI safety.

Leading the Future spent about $26 million in independent expenditures on the primaries alone. But spending tapered off as it headed into the general election, as the network dropped about $10 million in total while overwhelmingly backing candidates in safe races. Its funding also dropped off , with the network reporting zero donations in the second and third quarters.

The strategy seems to have shifted around the same time that stark polling began coming back showing widespread distrust of Big Tech and cronyism in Washington, DC. (An NBC exit poll found that 56 percent of voters said AI and data centers played a “major” role in their vote.)

Backing safe candidates was, simply put, “an influence play,” says Haworth. ”They're trying to ingratiate themselves with incoming members of Congress.”

The co-founder of Public First Action says that the midterms marked a victory for AI safety. “Voters in both parties delivered the same verdict tonight,” says Brad Carson. “This is a crushing blow to the AI industry’s anti-regulatory efforts to buy a Congress that would look the other way.”

Results weren’t great in the riskier races that Leading the Future jumped into.

One of its biggest bets was on Darline Graham, the sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham and an incumbent running to serve a full term in South Carolina. Graham earned the moniker “Data Center Darline ” from her Democratic opponent Annie Andrews due to her enthusiastic support of AI and data center expansion. American Mission donated more than $2 million to Graham, who ultimately lost with 46.5 percent in a state that last elected a Democrat to the Senate in 1998.

Of the other toss-up House races that Leading the Future weighed in on, almost all were in support of Republican candidates through the American Mission super PAC. The exception was Democratic Florida representative Jared Moskowitz’s reelection campaign, which it funded through Think Big. Moskowitz won by 13,000 votes against challenger Scott Singer, the former mayor of Boca Raton.

In North Carolina’s 1st congressional district, Leading the Future through American Mission backed Republican Laurie Buckhout, a retired Army colonel who served as an assistant secretary of defense working on cyber policy under President Donald Trump in 2025, in her primary. Guardrails Alliance, another player in the AI safety network, backed her opponent, Democrat Don Davis, who previously cosponsored a bill that would limit tax giveaways for data center development. Davis won.

Leading the Future also backed Aaron Flint, a retired combat veteran, conservative commentator, and former state director for Republican representative Ryan Zinke, who was running in Montana’s first congressional district. Flint conceded to his Democratic opponent Sam Forstag, a Democratic wildland firefighter who landed endorsements from major progressives including Alexandra Ocasio-Cortez and advocated for strict federal oversight of AI. (The Associated Press has yet to call the race.)

items.title: Gemini for Home now plugs into AT&T’s smart security system
items.summary: AT&T's smart home security system now integrates with Gemini for Home. The company says its Connected Life system is the "first" home security product to integrate with Google Home Premium, enabling a bunch of Gemini-powered features that can summarize home events, search your vi
items.content:
AT&T’s Connected Life system now supports Gemini-powered features that can summarize home events and more.

AT&T’s smart home security system now integrates with Gemini for Home. The company says its Connected Life system is the “first” home security product to integrate with Google Home Premium, enabling a bunch of Gemini-powered features that can summarize home events, search your video history, and more.

With the update, Gemini for Home can provide detailed descriptions about events captured by your security cameras, such as who delivered a package and how many items they dropped off. You can also search recorded video footage using natural language questions, like “What dug up the yard last night?” or “Who let the dogs out?”, as well as review daily summaries of activity in and outside your home.

These features are only available with AT&T’s professional $29.99 / month Connected Life monitoring plan. AT&T is also adding the ability to automatically arm or disarm your home based on your proximity to your home.

AT&T launched its Connected Life system last December in partnership with Google and Abode. It’s now taking advantage of Google’s Gemini-powered Home APIs , which allow smart home brands and developers to build AI-powered features into their devices. ADT has also hinted at bringing Gemini for Home features into its security systems.

items.title: Google Is Forcing AI Overviews in Classrooms. Schools Are Searching for a Way Out
items.summary: Google is tying up AI Overviews with traditional search, angering parents and educators who worry that easy, machine-generated answers are leaving kids less capable.
items.content:
Two weeks ago, an IT administrator for an elementary-middle school took to Google’s support forums requesting a way to block students from seeing AI Overviews —the chatbot-generated answers at the top of search results.

“This seems counterproductive to what we're trying to teach,” the administrator wrote . “Students need opportunities to navigate search results, examine sources, and draw their own conclusions rather than being handed an AI-generated synthesis before they've even started.”

No one from Google responded to the concern, which has been bubbling up for years. But counterparts from three districts voiced similar frustration and pointed to workarounds they were employing or considering to block AI Overviews in lieu of an official “off” switch. Their expertise is about to be in demand.

Google announced on Tuesday that it is declining to provide schools an option to disable AI Overviews . Instead, starting next year, schools will have to block access to search altogether to get rid of the feature. The decision has stunned educators, parents, and technology researchers across the US.

“We were flabbergasted,” says Dominique Johnson, part of an Oregon community group called Lake Oswego Parents For Responsible Technology. “This move makes things even more difficult for school districts that have determined AI is harmful to foundational learning.”

Google didn’t respond to a request for comment. But in a public response to the controversy shared on X, the company contended that schools will now have “more choice, not less” because search, its Gemini chatbot, and Gemini Notebook tool will be off by default starting next year. Administrators can enable one, two, or all three services.

The issue for schools and parents, though, is that Google considers AI Overviews and a companion feature called AI Mode inseparable from the traditional search experience. Respectively launched in 2023 and last year, they bring the functionality of AI chatbots, such as Gemini or ChatGPT, directly into search results.

“Kids are already using these search-bar summaries to skip real effort, pulling instant math answers and letting AI write their essays,” Johnson says. “To make matters worse, these AI snapshots frequently make mistakes and output false facts, which younger students take as absolute truth.”

The AI-generated responses are tempting to read and often good enough to trust , triggering headaches beyond classrooms. Wikipedia , news websites, and education tools have lost human visitors as people rely on overviews. Google uses the same bots to crawl the web for its search and AI products, making it impossible for publishers to opt out of their content being used for the latter.

Google’s push to make AI Overviews a prominent part of search has already come at a cost. Last week, shares of parent company Alphabet suffered their worst single-day selloff, erasing half a trillion dollars in market value after the company reported weaker-than-expected search ad sales. A big cause? Increased usage of AI Overviews and AI Mode, which aren’t packed with many ads yet—although some experts believe the slump will only be temporary.

For schools, the dilemma over search may be just beginning. While several districts WIRED contacted didn’t respond to requests for comment, Los Angeles Unified says it is still reviewing the potential implications of Google’s announcement. Some education technology experts argue that schools should abandon Google search altogether, or at least do a better job teaching students to question the validity of AI answers.

“Under-resourced districts will grit their teeth and say, ‘we don’t have the capacity to dig in our heels and not use Google,’” says Stephen Aguilar, who coleads University of Southern California’s Center for Generative AI and Society. “A lot are likely going to accelerate plans they already have to teach students about this new digital literacy.”

Parent advocates also plan to push districts to look elsewhere. “This move just continues a well-established pattern of big tech companies pushing products into classrooms,” says Karolle Rabarison, a policy and communications strategist who helps lead Schools Beyond Screens in Washington, DC. “It’s not going to work any more.”

Tech industry veterans disagree about how difficult it would be for Google to let schools disable AI Overviews without affecting the rest of Search. “It’s a question of whether they’re committed to maintaining two versions of search in the long run,” says Nicole Kerson, a former senior Google Search product manager who runs the AI strategy firm Collected Company. “It's very hard to maintain a forked product like that.”

Microsoft offers a Google Chrome extension that lets users turn off AI-generated summaries in Bing search. Adeel Khan, a former teacher and principal who now runs MagicSchool, which provides AI chatbots for students and teachers, says it is “infuriating, insulting, and ludicrous” that Google isn’t doing something similar.

Without an official way to disable AI Overviews, schools have turned to technical workarounds, including modifying search URLs and adopting browser extensions that change how Google results appear. Fairfax County Public Schools in Virginia recently developed its own extension . But these loopholes could stop functioning if Google changes how its search results are delivered.

Smaller search engines, such as the privacy-focused DuckDuckGo, see an opportunity to win business from schools frustrated with Google. “I wouldn't expect to see a Google-style ‘DuckDuckGo Classroom’ anytime soon, but ideally, we'll have special resources just for educators looking to make a switch,” says spokesperson Allison Goodman.

items.title: Knives Are Out in the White House
items.summary: From top officials like Pete Hegseth to White House aides to right-wing pundits, the race is on to find someone besides Donald Trump to blame for the Republicans’ catastrophic losses.
items.content:
President Donald Trump’s aides were reeling from the scale of Republican losses on Tuesday night, but they almost immediately began figuring out who to blame .

The ultimate responsibility, officials acknowledged only in private, lay with Trump for taking the country into an unpopular war with Iran that drove up prices, which became the number one issue for voters.

But in the absence of being able to blame Trump publicly, there has been growing pressure to find scapegoats in all places, from cabinet officials to White House aides to conservative media commentators.

Recalling how then-president George W. Bush pushed out defense secretary Donald Rumsfeld after the GOP lost both chambers in 2006, sources say there is an expectation from furious officials and donors for Trump to do something similar.

Trump does not seem to have made up his mind on whether he should, sources say, in part because of a recognition that there was perhaps not much that his staff could have done to stave off such overwhelming Democratic victories.

He has also been advised recently, sources tell Inner Loop , that it may be better to keep top staff inside the proverbial tent to ensure they remain loyal in the event they receive subpoenas from congressional investigators next year.

Still, some early scrutiny has been cast on people around Trump who have been viewed as encouraging the president to continue the Iran war even as it started to drag down polls months before the midterms.

Some scrutiny has been directed at defense secretary Pete Hegseth, who has been the target of a whisper campaign that he kept presenting rosy military outlooks that misled Trump into believing more strikes could win the war.

The presentations had been so glowing, sources say, that a number of top officials, including vice president JD Vance and secretary of state Marco Rubio this spring started requesting their own intelligence briefings to get a more somber assessment of the situation.

The Department of Defense did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

In other quarters, Trump advisers have been furious with conservative media commentators who they see as having encouraged the president to double down on the war even after it became mired in a stalemate over the Strait of Hormuz.

And still others returned to blaming White House deputy chief of staff James Blair, who temporarily left the administration to develop the GOP midterm strategy, including an effort to redraw congressional maps to favor Republicans.

In the end, that redistricting gambit backfired in epic fashion. Out of 14 key districts that got redrawn this cycle, Republicans won just one race in Texas and one race in Tennessee, while Democrats won most races in deep red Texas and Ohio by double digits.

Blair was already getting flak preemptively as polls ahead of the midterms showed Republicans down even in those races, some of which Trump carried by wide margins in the 2024 presidential election. But with many of the results now final, Blair has become a target, sources say.

Trump, for his part, spent the latter part of election night blaming the quality of candidates in key battleground races and claiming voters did not support Republicans because he was not on the ballot himself.

Still, other people in Trump’s orbit have been horrified but unsurprised that the president took no personal responsibility and denied that the devastating GOP losses were effectively a referendum on his second term.

Many of the candidates in key Senate races were people that Trump had chosen and endorsed, including the scandal-plagued Republican state attorney general Ken Paxton in Texas and the inexperienced Darline Graham, sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham, in South Carolina.

And in North Carolina, the former RNC chair Michael Whatley was defeated resoundingly by the Democratic Roy Cooper—but only after Trump primaried the popular incumbent Thom Tillis earlier this year.

As for Trump’s claim that he wasn’t on the ballot, that was undercut by the president explicitly telling voters at rallies across the country to pretend that he was, in order to drive turnout. And at those same rallies, some advisers noted, Trump overshadowed his own message by repeatedly talking about record profits of oil companies and his vanity construction projects.

Voters, it’s clear, didn’t like that message.

items.title: DuckDuckGo pitches itself to schools amid backlash over Google’s AI policy
items.summary: DuckDuckGo is courting schools frustrated by Google's AI restrictions, pointing educators to its search engine and options to disable AI features.
items.content:
DuckDuckGo is pitching itself to schools after Google created an opening for the alternative search engine. On Tuesday, Google told schools they could turn off Gemini , but it said shutting off its other AI features would cost schools Google Search , as well.

DuckDuckGo, a company that focuses on user privacy by limiting data collection, clearly sees this as a moment to make inroads in education, where Google has historically dominated. According to figures Google has published in previous years, there are around 50 million Chromebooks in schools, used by students and educators, and its Google Classroom platform serves over 150 million users globally.

On X , DuckDuckGo’s founder and CEO, Gabriel Weinberg, pointed to the company’s online documentation , explaining how schools can switch their default search engine to DuckDuckGo’s service instead, adding, “get in touch for help.”

Meanwhile, DuckDuckGo’s chief public affairs officer, Kamyl Bazbaz, issued a stronger statement, writing , “Forcing AI on school children: how a monopolist behaves when they think people are powerless. Prove Google wrong.”

Forcing AI on school children: how a monopolist behaves when they think people are powerless. Prove Google wrong. https://t.co/Ta6ibmFdb9

In an email to TechCrunch, DuckDuckGo chastised Google for its decision, adding that Google could easily turn off Search’s AI features for schools if it wanted to.

The company’s comments come as the American public is weighing how much AI they want to allow into their lives. As Tuesday night’s elections indicate, they don’t want AI data centers built in their towns. But using AI at work and school has become a common practice and requires a more nuanced discussion.

Knowing that educators have struggled with AI, Google developed technology called “ Guided Learning ” that is meant to help kids learn by walking through problem-solving steps rather than just providing them with an answer. But educators are still asking for tools that let them remove AI from the learning process altogether.

After the backlash on Tuesday, Google defended its decision, saying it was just responding to schools’ feedback. It said that Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search would be off by default, and schools could choose to enable them individually.

We want to clarify what we announced today about our education services. Today’s announcements give schools more choice, not less. Here’s what we announced: – Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be OFF 🔴 by default. This is based on K-12 schools asking for more control…

The problem, of course, is that Google Search now heavily uses AI, through AI Overviews and a conversational AI Mode that answers users’ queries.

DuckDuckGo isn’t anti-AI, to be clear — it offers its own set of AI features, including a chat interface called Duck.ai and an AI search assistant.

However, unlike Google, it provides options to disable these features in both its search and browser settings, the company says. It also offers a dedicated website, noai.duckduckgo.com , where AI-assisted answers, AI-generated images, and AI feature suggestions are all turned off.

That flexibility may be driving demand for its services, as the company reported earlier this year that its app installs were up 30% as users rejected being force-fed Google’s AI Search.
